<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914548_theRebbe_632" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914548_theRebbe_632__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces two interpretations of the statement that one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world surpasses all of the World to Come, explaining the relationship between repentance and good deeds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by first prefacing what our sages, of blessed memory, said:</t>
    <t s="2">"One hour of repentance and good deeds in this world is better than all the life of the World to Come."</t>
    <t s="3">And it is brought in Likkutei Torah</t>
    <t s="4">(in the discourses of Shemini Atzeret),</t>
    <t s="5">that "repentance and good deeds" has two explanations.</t>
    <t s="6">The first,</t>
    <t s="7">that the explanation of "repentance and good deeds" is that repentance is a preparation for good deeds,</t>
    <t s="8">for in order for the deeds to be good</t>
    <t s="9">(and illuminating)</t>
    <t s="10">it is through the precedence of repentance.</t>
    <t s="11">And accordingly,</t>
    <t s="12">this statement that "one hour... in this world" refers</t>
    <t s="13">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="14">to good deeds.</t>
    <t s="15">And although even according to this explanation there is a virtue in repentance, since it brings about good deeds,</t>
    <t s="16">this is in the manner of the known principle</t>
    <t s="17">regarding the matter of "Great is study that brings to action,"</t>
    <t s="18">that in this very thing the superiority of action is emphasized.</t>
    <t s="19">The second,</t>
    <t s="20">that repentance and good deeds are two separate matters,</t>
    <t s="21">and "one hour" refers to both of them,</t>
    <t s="22">that is,</t>
    <t s="23">repentance is a matter in and of itself.</t>
    <t s="24">And on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="25">repentance is more elevated than good deeds.</t>
    <t s="26">And accordingly, it can be said that the reason it places repentance before good deeds is because it is prior in level.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that both repentance and good deeds are forms of "return" (teshuvah)—repentance of the soul and repentance of the sparks—and that the superiority of one over the other depends on which aspect of teshuvah is emphasized.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the point of the explanation in this can be said to be that in both of them, it is the matter of teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="1">That is,</t>
    <t s="2">that even good deeds, their matter is teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="3">for through the fulfillment of the mitzvos</t>
    <t s="4">[and likewise through the service of "all your deeds shall be for the sake of Heaven,"</t>
    <t s="5">and all the more so</t>
    <t s="6">through "in all your ways know Him"]</t>
    <t s="7">one redeems the holy sparks within physical things and returns and elevates them to their source.</t>
    <t s="8">Except that teshuvah is the teshuvah of the soul,</t>
    <t s="9">the return of the soul to its source and root,</t>
    <t s="10">"and the spirit shall return to God who gave it,"</t>
    <t s="11">and good deeds are the teshuvah of the sparks of the world,</t>
    <t s="12">including also the sparks within his body and animal soul,</t>
    <t s="13">whose refinement and elevation is through the action of the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="14">good deeds.</t>
    <t s="15">And this is "one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world,"</t>
    <t s="16">for the matter of teshuvah</t>
    <t s="17">(the teshuvah of the soul,</t>
    <t s="18">and the teshuvah of the sparks,</t>
    <t s="19">good deeds)</t>
    <t s="20">is specifically in this world.</t>
    <t s="21">For this is the reason for the descent of the soul below,</t>
    <t s="22">in order that there should be in it the matter of teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="23">For when it is above, it is on the level of a tzaddik,</t>
    <t s="24">and through its descent below, the matter of teshuvah is renewed in it,</t>
    <t s="25">and "in the place where baalei teshuvah stand, even the completely righteous cannot stand."</t>
    <t s="26">And likewise regarding the descent of the sparks below,</t>
    <t s="27">that through their refinement and elevation</t>
    <t s="28">(the matter of the teshuvah of the sparks)</t>
    <t s="29">they are elevated higher than they were prior to the descent.</t>
    <t s="30">And accordingly, we can explain the two interpretations above regarding the fact that it places teshuvah before good deeds</t>
    <t s="31">[whether the main thing is good deeds and teshuvah is a preparation for good deeds,</t>
    <t s="32">or that the precedence of teshuvah to good deeds is also a precedence in level],</t>
    <t s="33">for in the elevation of teshuvah</t>
    <t s="34">(relative to tzaddikim)</t>
    <t s="35">there are several matters,</t>
    <t s="36">and there are matters whose essence is in the teshuvah of the soul,</t>
    <t s="37">and from the perspective of these matters,</t>
    <t s="38">teshuvah</t>
    <t s="39">(of the soul)</t>
    <t s="40">is prior in level to good deeds</t>
    <t s="41">(the teshuvah of the sparks),</t>
    <t s="42">and there are matters whose essence is in the teshuvah of the sparks,</t>
    <t s="43">and from this perspective the main thing is good deeds.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section details the superiority of simple repentance (for sins) over the service of tzaddikim, highlighting the greater thirst, the greater delight to God, and the leap-like, innovative nature of repentance.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing the superiority of simple repentance</t>
    <t s="2">(repentance for sins),</t>
    <t s="3">that it has several matters.</t>
    <t s="4">First,</t>
    <t s="5">that the thirst for G‑dliness of baalei teshuvah is a greater thirst than the thirst of tzaddikim.</t>
    <t s="6">For since beforehand they were distant,</t>
    <t s="7">therefore their thirst is greater,</t>
    <t s="8">as explained in Tanya.</t>
    <t s="9">And second,</t>
    <t s="10">that since beforehand they were distant,</t>
    <t s="11">the delight and satisfaction above that is brought about through repentance is greater than the delight and satisfaction of performing mitzvos</t>
    <t s="12">(the service of tzaddikim)—</t>
    <t s="13">"satisfaction"</t>
    <t s="14">"before Me that I spoke and My will was done."</t>
    <t s="15">And known is the parable of this, of a king's son who distanced himself from his father the king until he was in captivity, etc.,</t>
    <t s="16">that when he leaves captivity and comes to his father the king,</t>
    <t s="17">the delight and joy of them</t>
    <t s="18">(of the king's son and of the king)</t>
    <t s="19">is far greater than the delight and joy that there was beforehand</t>
    <t s="20">(before he distanced himself).</t>
    <t s="21">For the essence of delight and joy is from closeness that comes after distance.</t>
    <t s="22">And third,</t>
    <t s="23">that the service of teshuvah is in a manner of leap, not in order and gradation,</t>
    <t s="24">that one changes and becomes a new reality.</t>
    <t s="25">And in the language of the Rambam,</t>
    <t s="26">"I am another, and I am not the same person who did those deeds."</t>
    <t s="27">[And through this renewal</t>
    <t s="28">(of the person),</t>
    <t s="29">a renewal is also brought about in the world,</t>
    <t s="30">that intentional sins are transformed into merits.]</t>
    <t s="31">And from this as well, great delight is caused above,</t>
    <t s="32">for the essence of delight is specifically from something new,</t>
    <t s="33">as indicated by the well-known parable of the talking bird.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
